question_type: two-source composite: one Treasury Bulletin cell (MS-1, end-of-month currency) x an external BLS CPI-U year-over-year rate that is not in the corpus; round to 0.1 million
decisive_step: Interpretation, not lookup. Every solver that exists for this question (cells a, b, b2, c; the three v8 arms; the reference) read 'total currency in circulation' as the currency-only total column of Table MS-1 (not the grand total that also includes coin), took the latest printing, and multiplied by (1 + rate). All eight are graded wrong and all four cells sit in the same 5-25pct bin although their CPI rates differ by ~1.5 percentage points and all four lie within ~1.1% of the reference's own answer. So the key differs from the whole cluster by the interpretation, not by the CPI value: either the base column (currency+coin grand total, which is ~12-13% above the currency-only total) or the direction (deflating by (1+rate) instead of inflating, ~11% below). The reference made the column choice at solution.json decisions[0] / worklog Step 0(a) and the direction choice at solution.json decisions[3]; it flagged the grand-total reading as its main residual risk (review.md Verdict). A second, independent obstacle is that the CPI-U rate is external knowledge (worklog Step 5 confirms it is absent from the corpus): the four cells recalled four different index pairs, none matching the published figure the reference used.

a.path_summary: Found MS-1 via find_tables and printings (a[8], a[17]); at a[17]/a[18] weighed the currency-only total against the grand total (currency+coin) and, matching the question's word 'currency', chose the currency-only total at its latest printing (a[30]). Spent a[23]-a[37] and a[41]-a[47] searching the corpus and the Python environment for a CPI-U series (none exists), then reconstructed monthly CPI-U index values from memory by checking that they average to the annual figures it remembered (a[44]-a[48]) and settled on a rounded rate. Computed with calc (a[39]) and answered ~0.5% below the reference's value.

first_divergence.what_it_did: Read 'total currency in circulation' as the currency-only total column of MS-1 and 'applying the rate' as multiplying by (1+rate) - the same reading as the reference, which is graded wrong. Secondary divergence at a[44]-a[48] (EXTERNAL_KNOWLEDGE): reconstructed the CPI-U index from memory and got a rate ~0.5 points below the published one.
first_divergence.what_a_right_cell_or_the_reference_did: No cell and not the reference got this right. The key is 5-25% away from the entire cluster, consistent with the currency+coin grand total x (1+rate) or with the currency-only total / (1+rate).

smallest_change.change: No adapter change is supported by the evidence for the grade on this question. Two independent obstacles: (1) the key's reading of 'total currency in circulation' / 'inflation-adjusted' differs from the reading every solver chose, including the carefully reasoned reference, and the correct reading cannot be established from the corpus; (2) the CPI-U rate is external knowledge absent from the corpus, and GLM's recall is scattered (four cells, four different index pairs, none equal to the published figure the reference used). Fixing (2) alone still yields the reference's wrong answer.

alternatives.change: Ship the public BLS CPI-U monthly index (U.S. city average, all items, NSA, 1982-84=100) as a read-only series tool: `series cpi-u --month 1969-11 --yoy` prints three lines: 'CPI-U NSA 1968-11 = <index>', 'CPI-U NSA 1969-11 = <index>', '12-month change = <x.x>% (BLS published, rounded to 0.1) / <x.xxx>% unrounded'. Also mention it in README under Calculation.
alternatives.why_not_first: It would have collapsed the four-way rate scatter (a, b, b2, c all differ from the reference's rate) and saved 30-40 steps per cell, but would not have changed the grade here: the reference used the published rate and is still wrong. It is also benchmark-specific external data injected into the adapter, which is exactly what the clean-baseline argument wants to avoid; it is defensible only as public reference data, not as an evolved artefact.

alternatives.change: Header-shift detection in show_table/printings: when the identity check finds that column cK equals the row sum of c1..cK-1 on (nearly) all rows but the header's 'Total' label sits on another column, print under NOTES: 'HEADER SHIFT: label "Total currencies" is on c8 but c9 = sum c1..c8 on 24/24 rows; c9 is treated as Total currencies, c8 as the last component' and have --match/--col resolve 'Total currencies' to c9. printings should then align the row across issues by this role, so the Nov row prints as ONE value in every issue instead of '2 distinct values' (c8 in 7 issues, c9 in 5).
alternatives.why_not_first: All four cells ended on the arithmetic total anyway, so it would not have changed any answer here; but it would have removed b[31]'s wrong column, b's false 'revised from ... to ...' keep reason, b2[24]'s confusion, and the harness's first-printing offer to b. Confirmed defect: raw 1970_01 header (corpus line 1228) labels column 8 'Total currencies' and column 9 'Federal Reserve notes 4/' while the tool's own NOTES line at b[31] says 'c9 = sum c1..c8 on 24/24 rows'. document_qa_general, high confidence that it is real.

fix.why_not_text: Cell a (and c, b2) had the Provenance and Alternatives sentences and followed them as far as the corpus allows: they chose the base by wording and used calc. The two things that decide this question - the key's interpretation and the external CPI value - are not reachable by any sentence: the interpretation is one the reference reasoned about and rejected, and the CPI value does not exist in the corpus for any text to point at.
fix.irreducible: Yes for the grade: (i) the official answer uses a reading that eight independent solvers, including the strong reference, did not choose, and the alternative readings (grand total incl. coin, or deflation) are both defensible from the wording; (ii) the question requires an external BLS series that is absent from the corpus, so a corpus-only agent can only recall it, and GLM's recall of 1968-69 CPI-U index values is unreliable (spread of ~1.5 points in the rate across four cells). Not flagged issue47, but it behaves like a disputed item.

notes: 1) Confirmed tool defect worth fixing regardless of this question: the 1970_01 (and 1970_04-1970_09, 1971_01) OCR headers of MS-1 are shifted one column left, so show_table/printings label the Federal-Reserve-notes column 'Total currencies' while the tool's own identity check (NOTES: c9 = sum c1..c8 on 24/24 rows) proves the true total is the next column. printings therefore reports the same unrevised row as '2 distinct values' with 'first printing'/'latest printing' (a[17], b2[23], c[27]), and the mech harness offered the first-printing value to b as an alternative. All four cells happened to resolve it by taking the latest printing, but the same artefact on a question where the latest issue is the shifted one would push a 'latest printing' follower onto the wrong column. Aligning columns by the identity-derived role would fix both the label and the fake revision. 2) --grep matches only the raw row label ('Nov'), not the filled period (a[20], b[39], b2[13]); a hint line for 'line is inside a table' would have saved a[20]. 3) find_tables 'CPI' substring-matches FCPIX/FCP-II tables (112 parts of noise, a[17]). 4) Shell expansion of '$49,...' inside double quotes garbled b's first submit (b[46]); the recompute_final rule caught it. A submit note 'quote dollar amounts in single quotes' or having submit warn when the answer starts with ',' would avoid the round. 5) Cost of the external-data hunt: a ~20 steps, b2 ~40 steps (two loops), c ~35 steps (including reading tool-kit sources at c[51]); the reference settled 'not in corpus' in one grep + one FTS search (worklog Step 5). A one-line README note 'The corpus contains only Treasury Bulletins; it has no BLS/CPI series' would have cut this, but it is benchmark-specific text. 6) The reference's recall of the CPI index pair differed from all four GLM cells, and GLM's four attempts each reconstructed a different monthly series by matching remembered annual averages; recall is not a dependable path for this question type.
